name: António de Oliveira Salazar
role: Portuguese dictator, Prime Minister of Portugal 1932-1968, head of the Estado Novo (1889-1970)
summary: Salazar's own writings present the Estado Novo as a corporative, authoritarian state: parliamentary democracy and parties dissolved, class struggle rejected, family and religion as foundations, representation through corporations rather than parties, and the overseas provinces defended against self-determination claims.

sources.title: Como se levanta um Estado (Salazar, 1937; Internet Archive text; Portuguese original, translations are mine)
sources.author: António de Oliveira Salazar
sources.usedFor: His account of the Ditadura and the Estado Novo: parties, parliament, class struggle, family, corporative representation

sources.title: Discursos e Notas Políticas, 1928-1966 (Salazar; Internet Archive text; Portuguese original, translations are mine)
sources.author: António de Oliveira Salazar
sources.usedFor: His speeches and notes, including the Goa note and 'orgulhosamente sós'

sources.title: Constituição Política da República Portuguesa de 11 de Abril de 1933 (Diário do Governo, 22 Feb 1933; approved by plebiscite 19 Mar 1933, in force 11 Apr 1933 while he was Prime Minister; scan on parlamento.pt, Articles 1-23 read by OCR; translations are mine)
sources.author: República Portuguesa
sources.usedFor: The constitution of the Estado Novo: Arts. 5, 6, 8, 11-14, 21

property-fundamental.rationale: Article 8(15) of the 1933 Constitution lists among citizens' guaranteed rights 'o direito de propriedade e a sua transmissão em vida ou por morte, nas condições determinadas pela lei civil' (the right of property and its transmission in life or on death, under the conditions set by civil law), alongside the State's right under Article 6 to subordinate individuals to the general interest.

traditional-family.rationale: Article 11 of the 1933 Constitution says 'O Estado assegura a constituição e defesa da família, como fonte de conservação e desenvolvimento da raça, como base primária da educação, da disciplina e harmonia social, e como fundamento de toda a ordem política', and Article 12 founds the family 'no casamento e filiação legítima'; Article 13 tasks the State with protecting maternity and 'evitar a corrupção dos costumes'.

democracy-best.rationale: In Como se levanta um Estado (1937) he wrote that 'a democracia parlamentar conduziu por toda a parte à instabilidade e à desordem, ou então transformou-se numa espécie de dominação absoluta dos partidos sobre a verdadeira Nação' (parliamentary democracy led everywhere to instability and disorder, or became a kind of absolute domination of the parties over the true Nation), and called the English model unfit for all European peoples.

organic-representation.rationale: Article 5 defined the State as 'uma República unitária e corporativa', based on 'a interferência de todos os elementos estruturais da Nação na vida administrativa e na feitura das leis'; Article 11 grounds the political order on the family's 'agregação e representação na freguesia e no município', and Article 14 charges the State to recognise the moral and economic corporations and trade-union organisations and to promote their formation.

total-state.rationale: Article 6(2) of the 1933 Constitution charges the State to 'coordenar, impulsionar e dirigir todas as actividades sociais, fazendo prevalecer uma justa harmonia de interesses, dentro da legítima subordinação dos particulares ao geral' (coordinate, drive and direct all social activities, with the legitimate subordination of individuals to the general interest), while Article 8 keeps freedom of expression, religion and property 'nos termos que a lei determinar'.

national-self-determination.rationale: In his note on the Indian claim to Goa he called 'o pretenso direito da União Indiana a Goa' (the supposed right of the Indian Union to Goa), based among other things on 'o princípio da autodeterminação dos povos, ou seja, na vontade dos goeses', untenable, and defended keeping Portugal's overseas provinces, 'combatemos sem espectáculo e sem alianças, orgulhosamente sós'.

class-collaboration.rationale: In Como se levanta um Estado he wrote that the Estado Novo is 'contra o comunismo, contra o socialismo, contra o sindicalismo libertário, contra tudo o que diminui, divide, desagrega a família, contra a luta de classes' (against class struggle), and that his social reforms were won with no struggle against the employers' class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Article 5 of the 1933 Constitution denies privilege of birth, nobility, sex or social condition 'salvas, quanto à mulher, as diferenças resultantes da sua natureza e do bem da família' (except, for women, the differences resulting from their nature and the good of the family); Article 12 makes the spouses equal 'quanto à sustentação e educação dos filhos legítimos' only.

party-controls-media.rationale: Article 21 of the 1933 Constitution gave the press 'uma função de carácter público', by virtue of which it 'não poderá recusar, em assuntos de interesse nacional, a inserção de notas oficiosas' sent by the Government (it cannot refuse to print the Government's official notes on matters of national interest).

suppress-opposition.rationale: He described the Ditadura as 'encerramento e dissolução das Câmaras, dissolução dos partidos, instituição de um governo forte e independente, algumas outras restrições necessárias no tocante à liberdade de Imprensa e de reunião', arguing that giving the old parties freedom of action 'era permitir-lhes corromper a opinião pública e entravar toda a acção eficaz'.

notes: A new audit from two Portuguese-language texts on the Internet Archive: his 1937 book Como se levanta um Estado (the Estado Novo's 'dictionary', read by theme) and the 1928-1966 collection of speeches and notes (searched by theme: Goa, 'orgulhosamente sós', the death penalty, emigration, self-determination). Ten statements answered: six from the 1933 Constitution (Articles 1-23, read by OCR of the parlamento.pt scan: traditional-family, organic-representation, total-state, distinct-gender-roles, property-fundamental, party-controls-media) and four from his words (democracy-best, suppress-opposition, class-collaboration, national-self-determination); the rest of the 1933 Constitution (Articles 24 onward) and the Estado Novo's laws (the Estatuto do Trabalho Nacional, the Colonial Act) remain for a later pass to answer from acts. The uncertainty rule is not met.
